title: Bottlenecks to interstellar sulfur chemistry. Sulfur-bearing hydrides in UV-illuminated gas and grains
question: Whether gas-phase reactions of S atoms and SH+ molecules with vibrationally excited H2 can explain the presence of abundant H2S in FUV-illuminated gas, or if grain surface chemistry has to be invoked.

recipe.goal: Reduce and image ALMA, IRAM 30m, and SOFIA observations and extract line parameters
recipe.method: Combine ALMA 12 m mosaic and TP maps to synthesize 1'' SH+ cube, rotate image 37.5° clockwise, extract spectrum over a 5'' aperture toward the DF; reduce IRAM 30m position-switching spectra and OTF maps in GILDAS and convert to T_mb scale; reduce SOFIA/GREAT scans and calibrate to T_mb; smooth 4'' ACA+TP SH+ image to Herschel/HIFI beams to derive beam coupling factors f_b.
key_parameters: 5'' aperture toward (+10'', -10'') for ALMA SH+ line profiles
Beam coupling factors for Herschel/HIFI SH+: f_b ≃ 0.4 at ∼ 526 GHz and f_b ≃ 0.6 at ∼ 683 GHz
assumptions: T_ex = 10-30 K and extended emission for H3S+ upper limit

recipe.goal: Calculate ab initio state-dependent reaction rates for SH+ + H2(v) <-> H2S+ + H and S + H2(v) <-> SH + H
recipe.method: Compute >150,000 ab initio points with RCCSD(T)-F12a in MOLPRO to fit a 6D PES for H3S+(3A), then run ZPE-corrected quasi-classical trajectories (QCT) with miQCT to get SH+ + H2(v) and H2S+ + H rates; perform quantum wave packet calculations with MADWAVE3 on the Maiti et al. (2004) PES for S(3P) + H2(v) and SH + H.
key_parameters: Initial reactant distance = 85 bohr; minimum 10^5 trajectories per temperature in miQCT
Total angular momenta J = 0, 10, 20 with J-shifting interpolation in MADWAVE3
assumptions: Boltzmann distribution over translational and rotational degrees of freedom

recipe.goal: Derive single-slab non-LTE excitation and column densities of SH+, SH, and H2S
recipe.method: Solve statistical equilibrium and nonlocal radiative transfer with a Monte Carlo code including chemical formation pumping and destruction rates, dust continuum radiation, and inelastic collisions with H2, H, and e-.
key_parameters: Modified blackbody dust continuum at T_d ∼ 50 K with τ_λ = 0.03 (150/λ[µm])^1.6
T_form ≈ 2000 K for SH+; T_form = T_k for SH
assumptions: f(H2) = 2n(H2)/n_H = 2/3; n_e = 1.4x10^-4 n_H; H2 OTP ratio thermalized to T_k
SH-H and SH-H2 collisional rates scaled from SH-He rates by the square root of reduced mass ratios

recipe.goal: Model depth-dependent PDR chemistry and multi-slab radiative transfer for pure gas-phase and gas-grain networks
recipe.method: Run stationary isobaric PDR models of the Orion Bar (and constant-density models for general G0 and n_H) in the Meudon PDR code (v1.5.4) with updated gas-phase rates, wavelength-dependent photoreaction cross sections, and gas-grain / surface reactions (low E_b and high E_b); feed the depth-dependent PDR outputs into the multi-slab Monte Carlo radiative transfer code to predict emergent line intensities.
key_parameters: G0 = 2x10^4 Habing; A_V = 10 mag; P_th/k = 2x10^8 cm^-3 K; ζ_CR = 10^-16 H2 s^-1; R_V = 5.5; M_gas/M_dust = 100
Binding energies: low E_b/k (S = 1100 K, SH = 1500 K) vs high E_b/k (S = 2600 K, SH = 2700 K), E_b/k(H2S) = 2700 K; Y(H2S) = 1.2x10^-3 photon^-1
PDR inclination angle α = 5° (or 4° for column density table) vs face-on
assumptions: Grain size distribution n_gr ∝ a^-3.5; chemical desorption s-H + s-SH -> H2S efficiency of 50%; instant surface hydrogenation when τ_gr,H is shorter than sublimation/photodesorption timescales

score_reason: The paper provides complete spectroscopic line tables (Tables E.1-E.3), fitted Arrhenius reaction rate parameters (Table 1), PDR input parameters (Tables 2, 4), and ALMA project code, allowing partial reproduction of the chemical and excitation analysis; however, the nonlocal Monte Carlo radiative transfer code is not publicly released, ALMA calibration/imaging parameters are deferred to Goicoechea et al. (2016), and IRAM 30m/SOFIA data are not archived in the paper.
rediscovery_reason: ALMA dataset 2012.1.00352.S is public in the ALMA archive, the target coordinates and aperture (5'' around +10'', -10'' from the IF) are explicitly given, and the SH+ line intensities and column density are clearly quantified.
